--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.plot()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Render the graph as a static SVG image. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.plot()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Render the graph as a static SVG image. title: >- [Graph.plot()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Render the graph as a static SVG image. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Render the graph as a static SVG image. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4488-L4849){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.plot( layout="force", color_by=None, edge_color_by=None, size_by=None, label_by=None, edge_label_by=None, curved_edges=False, theme=None, palette="tableau", width=700, height=500, node_size=16.0, edge_width=1.2, edge_opacity=0.4, cross_community_color=None, node_overlap="remove", edge_routing="around", show_labels=True, output=None, seed=None, edge_width_by=None, color_scale=None, color_midpoint=None, highlight=None, highlight_edges=None, legend=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Produces a publication-quality SVG with filled-circle nodes, semi-transparent edges, optional community coloring, and light hover interactivity (tooltips). Visually consistent with the Cosmograph renderer used for large graphs. The drawing is computed entirely in Python/Rust, with no JavaScript layout step, so the result is a self-contained SVG that can be embedded in notebooks, Quarto documents, and web pages, or saved to disk. Node positions come from the chosen `layout=`, after which overlapping nodes are pushed apart and straight edges are routed around nodes that sit in their way. Directed graphs get arrowheads, parallel and reciprocal edges are fanned out as separate curves, and self-loops are drawn as small loops. Hovering over a node or edge in the HTML rendering shows its attributes. Aesthetics can be mapped from attributes: `color_by=` for node colors (a palette for groups, a color scale for numbers), `size_by=` for numeric node sizes, `label_by=` for the text shown on nodes, `edge_color_by=` to color edges by an edge attribute or by the groups of their endpoints, and `edge_width_by=` for numeric edge widths. A legend at the right explains the colors. `highlight=` and `highlight_edges=` pick out some nodes and edges, such as a path, in an accent color and mute the rest. This makes `plot()` a quick way to: - check the result of a community detection run - highlight important nodes by sizing or coloring them by a centrality score - show a path, a matching or a set of bridges within the whole graph - produce consistent figures for reports and documentation Attribute-based options read the attributes stored on nodes and edges (those set with `add_node()`, `set_node_attrs()`, or computed by methods like `betweenness_centrality()` and `cmty_louvain()`). `color_by=`, `size_by=` and `label_by=` also accept `"label"` (the node label, or the ID for unlabelled nodes), `"degree"` and `"id"` when no node has a stored attribute of that name; any other name that no node has raises a `ValueError`. The force and random layouts start from random positions, so pass `seed=` for a reproducible picture. For large graphs (several thousand nodes and up) consider `plot_cosmo()` instead. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [layout]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["force"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Layout algorithm. `"force"` (default) uses a Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed layout, which places connected nodes near each other. `"circular"` places nodes evenly on a circle in depth-first order (see `layout_circular()`), and `"random"` scatters them uniformly over the canvas. Any other string names a node attribute holding `(x, y)` positions, such as the `"pos"` attribute the `layout_*()` methods set; the positions are fitted to the canvas with `y` pointing up. `ValueError` is raised if some node lacks the attribute or doesn't hold two numbers. [color_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to map to colors (e.g., `"community"`, `"type"` or `"pagerank"`). How values become colors is set by `color_scale=`: by default, an attribute holding fractional numbers (floats) gets a sequential color scale, from light for the lowest value to dark for the highest, and any other attribute (strings, whole numbers such as community numbers, booleans) is taken as groups. Each group gets a color of `palette=`, in the sorted order of the values, and edges whose two endpoints share a group are drawn in that group's color. Nodes lacking a value are gray, with groups or on a color scale. Default is `None` (all nodes share one color). [edge_color_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : What to color edges by. The name of an edge attribute colors each edge by its value: fractional numbers get a sequential color scale (and edges are drawn more opaque, unless `edge_opacity=` is changed from its default), anything else a color of `palette=` per distinct value, and edges lacking the attribute keep the default edge color. Otherwise it names a node attribute, and edges are colored by the groups of their endpoints: an edge whose endpoints share a value gets that group's palette color, and an edge connecting two different groups (or a node with the attribute to one without it) gets `cross_community_color=`. When set, this takes precedence over the edge coloring done by `color_by=`. Like `color_by=`, it also accepts `"label"`, `"degree"` and `"id"`, and a name that no node or edge has raises `ValueError`. Default is `None`. [size_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Numeric node attribute to map to node radius, or `"degree"`. Values are min-max scaled so that radii range from half to twice the base `node_size=`. Nodes with a missing or non-numeric value get the base size. Default is `None` (uniform size). [label_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : What to display as the text on each node: `"id"` for the internal node ID, `"label"` for the node label (unlabelled nodes show their ID), or a node attribute name (nodes lacking it show their ID). If `None` (default), the attribute chosen with `set_node_attr_to_display()` is used, or `"id"` if none was chosen. Has no effect if `show_labels=` is `False`. [edge_label_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute to display as a small text label along each edge (e.g., `"rel"`), or `"weight"` for the edge weights. Edges without the attribute are left unlabelled. Default is `None` (no edge labels). [curved_edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, draw every edge as a quadratic Bezier curve instead of a straight line (edge routing is then skipped). Default is `False`. [theme]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Color theme, setting the background, default edge color, label color and tooltip styling: `"auto"`, `"light"` or `"dark"`. `"auto"` follows the color scheme of the page showing the plot (the light/dark toggle of a Quarto site, or a JupyterLab or VS Code theme), or else the system's, and switches along with it. If `None` (default), the plot is `"auto"` on screen while files written with `output=` or `save()` get the light theme, since programs other than browsers don't switch colors. Any other value raises `ValueError`. [palette]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["tableau"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of a color palette from `edgecase.colors` used for `color_by=` and `edge_color_by=` (see `edgecase.colors.list_palettes()` for the options, e.g., `"Set2"` or `"Dark2"`). Default is `"tableau"`. An unknown name raises a `ValueError` when `color_by=` or `edge_color_by=` is set. [width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[700]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : SVG canvas width in pixels. Default is `700`. Together with `height=`, it also influences the automatic node size. [height]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[500]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : SVG canvas height in pixels. Default is `500`. [node_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[16.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Base node circle radius in pixels. The default value, `16.0`, acts as "automatic": the radius is then derived from the canvas area and the number of nodes (between `3.5` and `16` pixels) so that nodes don't crowd each other. Any other value is used as given. [edge_width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.2]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge stroke width in pixels. The default value, `1.2`, acts as "automatic": small graphs get thicker edges (up to about 3 pixels) and large graphs thinner ones. Any other value is used as given, with a minimum of `0.5`. [edge_opacity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.4]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge stroke opacity, from `0` (invisible) to `1` (opaque). Default is `0.4`, which keeps dense regions readable. [cross_community_color]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Color (any SVG/CSS color string, e.g., `"#999999"` or `"red"`) for edges that connect different groups when `edge_color_by=` names a node attribute. If `None` (default), a neutral gray is used (`"#52525b"` in the light theme, `"#a1a1aa"` in the dark theme), so that it can't be mistaken for one of the groups' colors. Ignored unless `edge_color_by=` is set. [node_overlap]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["remove"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node overlap handling: `"remove"` (default) pushes overlapping nodes apart with a padding of 2 pixels (every layout but `"circular"`), `"allow"` keeps raw layout positions, or a number specifying the minimum padding (in px) between node circles. [edge_routing]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["around"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge routing for straight edges: `"around"` (default) bends edges around intermediate nodes with a 3 pixel clearance, `"straight"` draws direct lines, or a number specifying the clearance margin (in px) around nodes that edges must avoid. Routing only applies to graphs with at least 3 nodes and is skipped when `curved_edges=` is `True`. [show_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to display node labels (see `label_by=`). Default is `True`. [output]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional file path to save the output to. A path ending in `.html` saves the HTML version with hover tooltips; any other extension (typically `.svg`) saves the raw SVG. The rendered object is returned either way. Default is `None` (nothing is saved). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the `"force"` and `"random"` layouts. The same seed on the same graph gives the same positions. If `None` (default), positions differ between calls. [edge_width_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Numeric edge attribute to map to edge width, or `"weight"` for the edge weights (e.g., `"capacity"` or `"edge_betweenness"`). Values are min-max scaled so that widths range from half to two and a half times the base `edge_width=`. Edges with a missing or non-numeric value get the base width. A name that no edge has raises `ValueError`. Default is `None` (uniform width). [color_scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : How `color_by=` maps values to colors: `"categorical"` (a palette color per distinct value), `"sequential"` (a single-hue scale, light for low values and dark for high ones, for magnitudes like a centrality score) or `"diverging"` (two hues meeting at a neutral gray at `color_midpoint=`, for values with a sign or a meaningful middle, like a correlation). The two numeric scales need numeric values. If `None` (default), it's chosen from the values, as described under `color_by=`. In the dark theme the scales run the other way, so that high values stand out against the dark background. Any other value raises `ValueError`. [color_midpoint]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The value at the neutral middle of the `"diverging"` color scale. The scale extends equally far on both sides of it, so the more extreme side reaches the full color. If `None` (default), it's `0`. Ignored for the other scales. [highlight]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Nodes (and, through them, edges) to pick out: they are drawn in an accent color, or keep their `color_by=` color, while everything else is muted to gray. This can be a node ID or label; a list of them, where a list in which each node is adjacent to the next is taken as a path, whose edges are picked out too; `(u, v)` pairs in the list, for the edges between them; `"selection"`, for the selected nodes and edges; or the name of a node attribute, picking out the nodes that have a value for it other than `None`, `NaN` or `False` (a `0` counts). When the values are distinct whole numbers, the nodes are taken in their order as a path, so `highlight="shortest_path_order"` shows the path that `shortest_path()` found. The name of an edge attribute picks out the edges that have a value for it. For two levels of emphasis, pass a dict with the keys `"accent"` and `"soft"`, mapping each to such a value: soft nodes are drawn pale with an accent ring. Default is `None` (nothing is highlighted). [highlight_edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edges to pick out, as with `highlight=`, along with their endpoints: an edge ID, a list of edge IDs or of `(u, v)` pairs, a dict keyed by edge IDs (as `maximum_flow()` returns), `"selection"` for the selected edges, or the name of an edge attribute. It can be combined with `highlight=`, and also takes a dict with the keys `"accent"` and `"soft"`. What both levels pick out is drawn as accent. Default is `None`. [legend]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to show a legend at the right of the plot for the colors of `color_by=` and `edge_color_by=`: swatches for groups, or a color bar for a color scale. A legend for more groups than the palette has colors (or more than 12) is left out, since its colors would repeat. Default is `True`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [StepPlayer]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Interactive visualization that auto-renders in Jupyter notebooks (via `_repr_html_`) and can be saved with `.save(path)`. The raw SVG markup is available as its `.svg` property. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `color_by=`, `edge_color_by=`, `size_by=` or `label_by=` names an attribute that no node has (other than the built-in `"id"`, `"label"` and `"degree"`, and for `edge_color_by=` an edge attribute), `edge_width_by=` names an attribute that no edge has, `layout=`, `theme=` or `color_scale=` is unknown, a numeric `color_scale=` meets values that aren't numbers, `palette=` is unknown while `color_by=` or `edge_color_by=` is set, or `highlight=` or `highlight_edges=` names a node, edge or attribute the graph doesn't have. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~play`) : Replay the step log as an animation. [](`~plot_traversal`) : Step through a BFS or DFS one node at a time. [](`~record_traversal`) : Record a chain of traversals to step through. [](`~colorize_node_attrs`) : Store colors in a node attribute. [](`~describe`) : Print a summary of the graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Coloring by a community attribute is the most common use. Here Louvain communities are stored under `"community"` and each gets its own color; edges inside a community take that community's color: ::: {#b04fa7fe .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.karate_club().cmty_louvain(attr_name="community").plot( color_by="community" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Sizing by a centrality score makes the most important nodes stand out. In the karate club, the two largest nodes are the instructor and the administrator around whom the club eventually split: ::: {#60b25eca .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( ec.karate_club() .betweenness_centrality() .plot( size_by="betweenness_centrality", color_by="faction", show_labels=False, ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: For small graphs, attributes can supply readable node and edge labels. Labels come from the `name` attribute rather than the node ID, and each edge shows its `rel`: ::: {#66fa7bb4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes( [ ("a", {"name": "Ana"}), ("b", {"name": "Ben"}), ("c", {"name": "Cy"}), ] ) .add_edges( [ ("a", "b", {"rel": "manages"}), ("a", "c", {"rel": "manages"}), ("b", "c", {"rel": "mentors"}), ] ) ) graph.plot(label_by="name", edge_label_by="rel", layout="circular") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: `edge_color_by=` highlights the edges that cross between groups. Edges within a faction take the faction's color while the edges bridging the two factions are drawn in the `cross_community_color=`: ::: {#7134d29b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.karate_club().plot( color_by="faction", edge_color_by="faction", cross_community_color="black", edge_opacity=0.6, palette="Set2", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: A score with fractional values gets a color scale, explained by the color bar at the right. Here PageRank both colors and sizes the characters of *Les Misérables*: ::: {#bfb38a40 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.les_miserables().pagerank().plot( color_by="pagerank", size_by="pagerank", seed=1 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: `highlight=` picks out part of the graph and mutes the rest. Given the attribute that `shortest_path()` stores, it shows the path it found, nodes and edges alike: ::: {#45b0bd1b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( ec.metro() .shortest_path("Westgate", "Airport") .plot(highlight="shortest_path_order", label_by="label", seed=3) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Curved edges and the dark theme give a different look: ::: {#0d1d36f4 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.dolphins().plot(layout="force", curved_edges=True, theme="dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Static plots](../user-guide/plotting.qmd#a-first-plot) draws the karate club, and then covers saving, labels, layouts, curved edges, themes and larger graphs.
